welcome.label: Welcome · the backup light

parts.label: 🛠️ You are the engineer
parts.title: Design a backup light
parts.body: Goals, limits, a prototype, a test and a redesign.

welcome.script:
(Hold up a paper airplane, throw it, and watch it nosedive.) Hmm. Did I fail? Or did I just learn something?

[ON SCREEN: The storm watch]
The jetty light is fixed, but a storm is coming, and clouds will hide the Sun for days.

[ON SCREEN: You are the engineer]
Today you design a backup light. Read the storm watch and the keeper’s note in the case file just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · stamp the work order (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Hold up a backpack.) If I design a backpack, “holds my books” is a goal. “Costs under 20 dollars” is a limit.

[ON SCREEN: The work order]
Goals are criteria. Limits are constraints. Stamp each line of the keeper’s work order. Press Listen on Sam’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

part1.label: Part 1 · limits cross out ideas (Clue 2)

parts.label: ✂️ Limits cross out ideas
parts.title: 6 ideas, 3 limits
parts.body: Add one limit at a time. Which ideas survive?

part1.script:
Six ideas for a backup light. Some can’t possibly work here.

[ON SCREEN: Limits cross out ideas]
Add the keeper’s limits one at a time and watch which ideas get crossed out. Limits save you time!

part2.label: Part 2 · the version timeline (Clue 3)
part2.script:
[ON SCREEN: The version timeline]
Sam’s first backup light failed. Read the test results and pick the ONE change that fixes it. Why only one?

[ON SCREEN: Even the Wright brothers]
The Wright brothers’ 1901 glider disappointed them, too. They didn’t quit. They tested and redesigned. Press Listen.

explore.label: Part 3 · design it, then storm it (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Cup your hands like you’re holding something precious.) Now it’s YOUR light.

[ON SCREEN: Design it, then storm it]
Pick an energy input and add-ons, stay under fifty dollars, and run the storm test. Did it go dark? Good. Now you know what to fix.

[ON SCREEN: Redesign pays off]
The Wrights’ redesigned 1902 glider flew beautifully. Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Ready for the storm?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: 📐 Your patent drawing
parts.title: Name it and stamp it
parts.body: Your storm-test design becomes a patent drawing.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Four clues: crack the case at the top of this tab.

[ON SCREEN: Your patent drawing]
Then your storm-test design becomes a patent drawing. Give it a great name!

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Last, two short answers, your design plan with a labeled sketch, and your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “Real engineers come up with perfect designs on their first try.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
Perfect on the first try? Think about your own storm test. Did yours pass the first time?

There’s no wrong side, as long as you prove it.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts, then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 📐 Your specimen
parts.title: Your approved patent drawing
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

closing.script:
(Throw a second, better paper airplane that glides.) Version two!

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and your patent drawing goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time: sound. Put your fingers on your throat and hum. Feel that? We’ll find out what it is.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
